[P1] 金瓜儿
银豆儿
毛毛虫童书馆
赵燕翼 文
柯明 图
新蕾出版社
赵燕翼 文

[P4] 柯明 (1932— )
    原名吴樾人，青年时曾就读于国立
艺专，学习西洋画，后自学木版年画、剪
刻纸、皮影、泥塑等传统民间美术。曾长
期工作和生活在南京，为美术电影《红军
桥》、动画片《天书奇谭》、木偶片《曹
冲称象》做人物造型设计。《金瓜儿银豆
儿》获联合国教科文组织野间奖。

[P5] 金瓜儿 银豆儿
赵燕翼/文
柯明/图

[P6] 河西走廊铁柜山，山下住着老两口。老两口开了一块荒地，栽种蔬菜瓜豆，过着苦日子。
这一年，天气大旱。天上不下雨，河里水晒干；种子不发芽，苗儿不出土。春天过去了，老两口的菜园，还是一块白地。他俩好忧愁啊，不住地唉声叹气！

[P8] 有一天，忽然发现自己的菜园里，有两棵茁壮的嫩芽芽，顶破干硬的地皮，
迎着炎炎烈日，冒出来了。一棵芽芽粉红，一棵芽芽翠绿。老两口好欢喜啊！
早松土，晚锄草，十里路担来清泉水，一勺一勺舀着浇；这两棵稀罕的
芽芽啊，一天比一天长得高。

[P9] 红芽芽长了八尺八，蔓蔓爬上葫芦架。生绿叶，
开黄花；黄花落了，结了一个大金瓜。
绿芽芽长了三尺三，长长的秧儿南墙上牵。开
的什么花？粉红花。结的什么果？银豆角。豆角有
多少？只有一个，像弯弯的月牙儿。
三月出芽，四月生叶，五月开花，六月结果。
七月八月，瓜儿熟了，豆角饱了。老两口儿，选了
一个风和日暖的好天气，来到菜园里，一个去摘金瓜，
一个去采豆角。

[P10] 老头儿走到瓜架下，还没有动手摘哩，金瓜自己落地了；老婆儿走到豆棚前，还没有动手采哩，银豆角自己离秧了。
瓜儿落下地，一分两瓣，瓜壳里睡着一个憨敦敦的胖娃娃。
豆角离了秧，裂开口儿，豆荚里躺着一个嫩生生

[P11] 的俊女儿。老两口大吃一惊，回头便跑，只听后面
连声叫：
“爹爹，爹爹，您别害怕，我是您的亲娃娃！”
“妈妈，妈妈，您莫惊疑，我是您的亲女儿！”
“妈妈”“爹爹”，“爹爹”“妈妈”，一声，两声，

[P12] 三声，叫得那么亲热，叫得那么甜蜜。叫得老两口站住脚，叫得老两口回了头，直叫得老两口眉开眼笑走上前。老头儿抱起金瓜壳里的男孩儿，老婆儿抱起银豆荚里的女孩儿。老两口好欢喜啊，他们也有了儿女。
男孩儿取个啥名儿？老头儿说：“就叫金瓜儿！”女孩儿取个啥名儿？老婆儿说：“就叫银豆儿！”
金瓜儿，银豆儿    喔！一对可爱的小儿女，都有了自个儿好听的名儿！

[P13] 只愁生不下，不愁长不大。转眼几年，金瓜儿银豆儿都长大成人了。

[P14] 金瓜儿帮爹爹种菜。别看他人小，本领可不小：种苹果，栽葡萄，樱桃颗颗赛玛瑙；菠菜韭菜一片绿，紫花茄子红辣椒……破破烂烂的小菜园，变成整整齐齐的花果园。看风景，美得很，论出产，富得很。春种秋收，不用爹爹再操心。

[P15] 银豆儿帮妈妈管家。她手脚勤，心眼儿灵：论针线，比裁缝；论茶饭，胜厨子；论力气，赛男儿。南山打柴，西河担水；碾下的米，珍珠黄；磨下的面，雪花白。她又养鸡鸭又养鹅……家中事不论大小，安排得井井有条，不用妈妈再操劳。有了这一对能干的儿女，老两口欢欢乐乐，过着好光景。

[P16] 这一年，金瓜儿的菜园里，结了个出奇的大冬瓜，长得像碌碡那么大，像碧玉那么光滑。金瓜儿在冬瓜上面刻了四个字：冬瓜王子。

[P17] 银豆儿的鸡群里，出了只罕有的大公鸡，脚爪像一双铁钩，羽毛像美丽的彩霞，头顶的鸡冠，像一朵大红花。一声长鸣，能唤出东海的太阳，展翅高飞，能直上九天云外。银豆儿给公鸡脖子上挂一面小牌牌，上面写了四个字：雄鸡将军。

[P18] 南庄有个李员外，有一天，他骑马路过铁柜山，猛看见这山下美丽的花果树木，一心想霸占。他说：“这是我的地界，谁在这里种菜？”左右跟班一打听，领来白发苍苍两老人。李员外对老头儿说：“这山，是李家山，这地，叫李家园。你们在我的园地上种菜栽树，为什么不纳粮交租？”
老头儿一听生了气，说：“这山，原是个荒草山；这地，原是个石头滩。我辛勤劳动四十年，才开下这一片花果园！

[P19] 老婆儿接着说：“这菜，是我女儿种的；这树，是我儿子栽的。我们就是这里的园主，为什么要给你纳粮交租？
“你们的儿女在哪里？赶快把他们叫出来！
“我们的女儿叫银豆儿，我们的儿子叫金瓜儿。一个去砍柴，一个去卖瓜，他们恰巧不在家。”
“不在也罢，就和你们说话。”李员外冷笑一声说：“官凭印，虎凭山，土地要由契约管。你们既是园主，手里可有地契？
地契？没有。老两口你望我，我望你，说不出一句话。

[P20] “你没地契，我有地契。种了我的园子四十年，官粮地租，从头清算！”李员外这么一说，随身的管家，端起算盘一拨拉，算下黄金白银各十两。“黄金白银，限你们三天交清。交不出金银，把你们一家赶出门！
李员外走了，老两口心里好愁闷，三天期限，哪里去变二十两金银？金瓜儿银豆儿回家来，听说这件事，心里很气愤。可是，看着爹妈愁眉苦脸，只好安慰两位老人说：“爹爹妈妈不用愁，咱们有两双劳动的手，能从没有变出有。人人都说，铁柜山里金银多，咱们俩登山寻宝，一定要把黄金白银找到！”
金瓜儿银豆儿来到铁柜山，镢头挖，铁锨铲，手心打起血泡，脸上流着热汗。

[P23] 熬了两天两夜，挖出的沙石堆成岭，却找不见一点儿金和银！兄妹俩实在太累了，
坐下来想缓口气儿。就在这时候，忽然从天空飞来一只大鸟，抡开利爪，抓住山头，
“轰隆”一声，把一座铁柜山，悬空提起几丈高；接着，又突然“咕咚咚”一阵响，
从远处滚来一块大石头，稳稳地支在山底下。

金瓜儿银豆儿见了这般情景，心里又惊又喜，连忙跑到山下一看：呀！黄灿
灿的，是金山；白花花的，是银山；还有聚宝盆，珊瑚树，琥珀玛瑙夜明珠……
把人的眼睛都耀花了！

金瓜儿在金山上，捡了一块金子；银豆儿在银山上，拾了两锭银子。他们说：
“这就够交租了，咱们走吧。”

[P25] 兄妹俩刚从山底下跑出来，忽见那块支山石头，骨碌碌碌滚过来，直滚到金瓜儿面前。仔细一看，上面刻着四个字：冬瓜王子　　原来是金瓜儿亲手种下的那个大冬瓜！接着，那抓山大鸟，稳稳地放下铁柜山，扑啦啦啦飞下来，直飞到银豆儿身边。仔细一看，大鸟脖颈上挂着块牌牌：雄鸡将军　　原来是银豆儿喂的那只红公鸡。
金瓜儿抱起他的大冬瓜，银豆儿抱起她的红公鸡，兄妹俩心里好欢喜：“啊哈，支山冬瓜抓山鸡，原来出在咱家里！”

[P26] 第三天，李员外收租来了，兄妹俩又不在家。老两口拿出了一块金，两锭银，称一称：黄金十两，白银十两，不多一丝，不差半分。李员外心里好奇怪：这穷汉家里，哪来这么多金银？便问老两口：“你这金银，是哪里来的？说明来路，我才能收！”老两口都是老实人，便把实情一五一十说明。

[P27] 李员外一听，心里另打坏主意。他不收金，不收银，却要拿这菜园子，来换支山冬瓜抓山鸡。老两口连连摇头不答应。李员外眼一翻，脸一沉，说道：“冬瓜是我地里长的，公鸡是我粮食喂的。好心赏你们便宜，你们还不识抬举！来人啊，把冬瓜公鸡给我收回去！”管家跟班一声喊，抱去了大冬瓜，抢走了红公鸡。

[P29] 金瓜儿卖菜回家了，银豆儿担水进门了。
只见爹爹唉声叹气，妈妈抹泪哭泣；一问原因，才知道是李员外夺走了支山冬瓜抓山鸡。
兄妹俩一听，怒火心头起：“李员外这只老狼，我们开下荒地，他要收租；给他交了租，他又夺去咱们的宝瓜神鸡！爹爹别发愁，妈妈莫流泪，我们追上前去，和他评一评道理。他要不讲理，我们活活剥下他的老狼皮！”
说罢，金瓜儿提上他挖地的镢头，银豆儿拉起她担水的扁担，兄妹俩出了门，直向大路上追赶。
李员外领着跟班管家，来到铁柜山下。放出抓山公鸡，抓起铁柜山；抛出支山冬瓜，支在山底下。他们一窝蜂拥上前，围着金银宝贝打转转。想抬走金山，又舍不得银山；双手抱住珊瑚树，眼睛瞅着夜明珠；还有琥珀、玛瑙、水晶、白玉……都想搬回家里去。就在这时，金瓜儿银豆儿赶来了。
金瓜儿银豆儿，一见李员外这伙坏蛋，在山底下闹闹嚷嚷，乱作一团，又是厌恶又是气。金瓜儿朝山底下招招手，高声叫道：
“冬瓜王子，冬瓜王子！快回来，快回来，别让贪心鬼发横财！”
支山冬瓜一听是小主人的声音，离开山底下，骨碌碌碌滚回来。

[P31] 银豆儿向天空招招手，也高声叫道：
“雄鸡将军，雄鸡将军！把山丢下，把山丢下，贼人来偷宝，
快快压死他！”
抓山鸡听见小主人唤它，丢下铁柜山，扑啦啦啦飞回来。
只听得“轰隆”一声震天响，铁柜山从半悬空中落下来，原样
儿合在一起了。那伙仗势欺人的坏蛋，永远永远压在山底下了。
full_text_en:
[P1] Golden Gourd, Silver Bean
Caterpillar Children's Library
Written by Zhao Yanyi
Illustrated by Ke Ming
New蕾 Publishing House
Written by Zhao Yanyi

[P4] Ke Ming (1932— )
    Originally named Wu Yue-ren, he studied Western painting at the National Art College in his youth, and later taught himself traditional folk arts such as woodblock New Year paintings, paper cutting, shadow puppetry, and clay sculpture. He worked and lived in Nanjing for a long time, designing character models for the art film "The Red Army Bridge," the animated film "The Legend of the Book of Heaven," and the puppet film "Cao Chong Weighs the Elephant." His work "Golden Gourd, Silver Bean" won the UNESCO Wilder Prize.

[P5] Golden Gourd, Silver Bean
Zhao Yanyi / Text
Ke Ming / Illustrations

[P6] In the Hexi Corridor, at Tiegui Mountain, an old couple lived at the foot of the mountain. They cleared a patch of wasteland and planted vegetables, melons, and beans, living a hard life.
That year, there was a severe drought. No rain fell from the sky, and the river water dried up; seeds didn't sprout, and seedlings didn't emerge from the soil. Spring passed, and the old couple's vegetable garden was still a barren patch. They were deeply worried, constantly sighing and groaning!

[P8] One day, they suddenly discovered two sturdy little sprouts in their vegetable garden, breaking through the hard ground and emerging under the scorching sun. One sprout was pink, the other was emerald green. The old couple was overjoyed!
They loosened the soil in the morning, weeded in the evening, carried clear spring water from ten miles away, and watered them spoon by spoon. These two rare sprouts grew taller and taller each day.

[P9] The red sprout grew eight feet eight inches, its vines climbing up the gourd trellis. It grew green leaves, 
then yellow flowers; when the flowers fell, a big golden gourd formed.
The green sprout grew three feet three inches, its long vines trailing along the southern wall. What 
flowers did it bloom? Pink-red flowers. What fruit did it bear? Silver beans. How many beans? 
Only one, shaped like a crescent moon.
In March, it sprouted; in April, it grew leaves; in May, it bloomed; in June, it bore fruit.
In July and August, the gourd ripened, and the beans filled up. The old couple chose 
a fine, warm, sunny day to go to the vegetable garden, one to pick the golden gourd, 
the other to harvest the beans.

[P10] The old man walked under the melon trellis, hadn't even started picking yet, when the golden melon fell to the ground by itself; the old woman walked to the bean trellis, hadn't even started harvesting yet, when the silver bean pod fell off the vine by itself.
The melon fell to the ground, split into two halves, and inside the shell slept a plump, chubby baby.
The bean pod fell from the vine, split open, and inside the pod lay a tender, fresh baby.

[P11] The beautiful daughter. The old couple was greatly startled and turned to run, only to hear voices calling from behind:
"Dad, dad, don't be afraid, I'm your own little one!"
"Mom, mom, don't be alarmed, I'm your own daughter!"
"Mom" "Dad", "Dad" "Mom", one call, then two calls,

[P12] Three calls, so affectionate, so sweet. They made the old couple stop in their tracks, turn around, and finally walk forward with beaming smiles. The old man picked up the boy from the golden gourd shell, and the old woman picked up the girl from the silver bean pod. How happy the old couple was—they now had children!
What should we name the boy? The old man said, "Let's call him Jin Guer!" What should we name the girl? The old woman said, "Let's call her Yin Douer!"
Jin Guer, Yin Douer—Oh! A lovely pair of children, each with their own beautiful name!

[P13] Only worried about not being able to have children, never worried about them not growing up. In no time, Jin Guer and Yin Douer had grown into adults.

[P14] Jin Guer helps his father grow vegetables. Don't look at his small size, his skills are great: planting apples, growing grapes, cherries as shiny as agates; spinach and chives a lush green, purple eggplants and red peppers... the once shabby little vegetable garden has become a neat and tidy fruit and vegetable garden. In terms of scenery, it's very beautiful; in terms of yield, it's very rich. Spring planting, autumn harvest, no need for father to worry anymore.

[P15] Yin Dou'er helps her mother manage the household. She is diligent and clever: her needlework rivals that of a seamstress; her cooking surpasses that of a chef; her strength matches that of a man. She fetches firewood from the southern mountain and carries water from the western river; the rice she grinds is as golden as pearls, and the flour she mills is as white as snow. She raises chickens, ducks, and geese... every household task, big or small, is arranged neatly, so her mother no longer needs to worry. With such capable children, the elderly couple lives happily and joyfully, enjoying a good life.

[P16] This year, in Jin Guer's vegetable garden, a remarkably large winter melon grew, as big as a碌碡 and as smooth as jade. Jin Guer carved four characters onto the melon: 'Winter Melon Prince.'

[P17] In Yindou'er's flock of chickens, there appeared a rare big rooster. Its claws were like iron hooks, its feathers like beautiful rosy clouds, and its comb on top of its head looked like a big red flower. With one long crow, it could call forth the sun from the East Sea; with its wings spread wide, it could fly straight up to the clouds of the ninth heaven. Yindou'er hung a small plaque around the rooster's neck, on which were written four characters: 'General Rooster'.

[P18] In the southern village, there was a rich man named Li. One day, while riding his horse past Tiegui Mountain, he suddenly saw the beautiful fruit trees below and wanted to take them over. He said, “This is my territory. Who is planting vegetables here?” After asking his followers, they brought back two elderly people with white hair. Li said to the old man, “This mountain is Li’s Mountain, and this land is Li’s Garden. Why aren’t you paying rent for planting vegetables and trees on my land?”
The old man got angry and replied, “This mountain was once a barren grassy hill; this land was once a rocky beach. I worked hard for forty years to turn it into this fruit garden!”

[P19] The old woman continued, "These vegetables were planted by my daughter; these trees were planted by my son. We are the rightful owners of this garden. Why should we pay you rent and taxes?"
"Where are your children? Bring them out quickly!"
"Our daughter is named Yindou'er, and our son is named Jingua'er. One is chopping firewood, the other is selling melons. They just happen to be away from home."
"Well, if they're not here, I'll speak with you." Li Yuanwai sneered, "Officials rely on seals, tigers rely on mountains—land must be governed by contracts. You claim to be the owners, but do you have a land deed?"
"A land deed? No. The old couple looked at each other, speechless.

[P20] "You have no land deed, I have a land deed. You've cultivated my garden for forty years, now we'll settle the official grain and land rent from the beginning!" Upon saying this, Li Yuanwai's attendant took out an abacus and calculated ten taels of gold and ten taels of silver. "Gold and silver, you must pay it all within three days. If you can't pay, I'll evict your whole family!"
Li Yuanwai left, and the elderly couple felt deeply distressed. How could they come up with twenty taels of gold and silver in three days? When Jin Guer and Yin Douer heard about this, they were very angry. But seeing their parents' worried faces, they comforted the two elders, saying, "Don't worry, Dad and Mom. We have two pairs of hardworking hands. We can turn nothing into something. Everyone says there's plenty of gold and silver in Tiegui Mountain. Let's climb the mountain and search for treasure. We must find the gold and silver!"
Jin Guer and Yin Douer arrived at Tiegui Mountain, digging with hoes and shoveling with iron shovels, their palms blistered and sweat streaming down their faces.

[P23] They had endured two days and two nights, piling up sand and stones into hills, yet found not a single bit of gold or silver! The brother and sister were utterly exhausted, sitting down to catch their breath. Just then, a huge bird suddenly flew down from the sky, spread its sharp claws, grabbed the mountain peak, and with a '轰隆' (hōng lōng) sound, lifted the entire Iron Cabinet Mountain several zhang high into the air; then, suddenly, a '咕咚咚' (gū dōng dōng) rumbling sound came, and a huge stone rolled from afar, steadily supporting the mountain from below.

Jin Guer and Yin Douer, seeing this scene, were both amazed and delighted. They rushed to the foot of the mountain and exclaimed: "Wow! The golden, shining mountain is a gold mountain; the white, gleaming one is a silver mountain; and there are also treasure basins, coral trees, amber, jade, and night pearls... dazzling the eyes!"

Jin Guer picked up a piece of gold from the gold mountain; Yin Douer picked up two ingots of silver from the silver mountain. They said: "This is enough to pay the rent. Let's go!"

[P25] The brother and sister had just run out from the bottom of the mountain when they saw the mountain-supporting stone rolling over, bumping straight to Jin Guer's front. Upon closer look, it had four characters carved on it: 'Winter Melon Prince' — it was the big winter melon that Jin Guer had planted himself! Then, the mountain-carrying big bird steadily put down the Iron Cabinet Mountain, flapping down and flying straight to Yin Douer's side. Upon closer look, the bird had a sign hanging around its neck: 'Rooster General' — it was the red rooster that Yin Douer had raised!
Jin Guer picked up his big winter melon, and Yin Douer picked up her red rooster. The siblings were overjoyed: "Ah ha, the mountain-supporting winter melon and the mountain-carrying rooster — they came from our own home!"

[P26] On the third day, Mr. Li came to collect rent, but the siblings were not at home. The elderly couple took out a piece of gold and two ingots of silver. They weighed them: ten taels of gold, ten taels of silver, not a thread more, not a fraction less. Mr. Li was very curious: 'How could such a poor household have so much gold and silver?' He asked the couple, 'Where did you get this gold and silver? Explain its origin, or I cannot accept it!' The couple were honest people, so they told the truth in full detail.

[P27] Upon hearing this, Master Li had a different, wicked idea. He didn't want gold or silver, but instead wanted to take their vegetable garden in exchange for the mountain-holding winter melon and the mountain-carrying rooster. The old couple shook their heads repeatedly, refusing. Master Li rolled his eyes, his face darkening, and said: "The winter melon grew on my land, and the rooster was fed with my grain. I'm doing you a favor by offering it cheaply, and you still don't know how to appreciate it! Someone, bring back the winter melon and rooster for me!" The steward and servant shouted, grabbed the big winter melon, and snatched the red rooster.

[P29] Jin Guer came home from selling vegetables, and Yin Douer entered the door carrying water.
They saw their father sighing and their mother crying; upon asking the reason, they learned that Li Yuanwai had taken away the mountain-supporting winter melon and the mountain-grabbing rooster.
Hearing this, the siblings were furious: "Li Yuanwai, this old wolf! We cleared the wasteland, and he demands rent; after we paid the rent, he stole our magical melon and rooster! Father, don't worry, Mother, don't cry. We'll chase after him and reason with him. If he refuses to listen, we'll peel off his old wolf skin!"
After saying this, Jin Guer picked up his hoe, and Yin Douer grabbed her water-carrying pole. The siblings left the house and rushed down the road to chase after him.
Li Yuanwai, leading his lackeys and steward, arrived at the foot of Tiegui Mountain. He released the mountain-grabbing rooster, lifted the mountain, threw out the mountain-supporting winter melon, and placed it under the mountain. They rushed forward like a swarm, circling around the gold and silver treasures. They wanted to carry away the gold mountain but couldn't bear to leave the silver mountain; they hugged coral trees with both hands, their eyes fixed on the night pearls; and they wanted to take home amber, agate, crystal, jade... everything. Just then, Jin Guer and Yin Douer arrived.
Jin Guer and Yin Douer, seeing Li Yuanwai and his gang making a ruckus at the foot of the mountain, were disgusted and angry. Jin Guer waved his hand toward the mountain base and shouted loudly:
"Winter melon prince, winter melon prince! Come back, come back, don't let the greedy scoundrel get rich!"
The mountain-supporting winter melon, hearing the voice of its young master, left under the mountain and rolled back, bumping along.

[P31] Yindou'er waved to the sky and shouted loudly:
"Rooster General, Rooster General! Drop the mountain, drop the mountain, thieves are stealing treasure,
Quickly crush them!"
The mountain-rooster heard its young master calling and dropped the Iron Cabinet Mountain, flying back with a flutter.
A thunderous "Boom" echoed through the sky as the Iron Cabinet Mountain fell from mid-air, rejoining perfectly.
Those bullies who took advantage of others were forever and ever buried beneath the mountain.

[P3] 本页为纯黄色背景，横向排列着五个剪纸风格的图案，包括一朵紫色花朵和三只粉色蝴蝶，整体风格简洁，无文字内容。
[P4] 本页展示了插画师柯明的黑白肖像及其生平简介，介绍了他的艺术背景、代表作品及所获荣誉。
[P5] 本页为绘本《金瓜儿银豆儿》的封面，展示了书名、作者赵燕翼和插画师柯明的信息，画面中有两个婴儿分别坐在绿色豆荚和紫色南瓜上，周围环绕着花朵和藤蔓，背景为深蓝色。
[P6] 本页介绍了故事背景：在河西走廊铁柜山下，一对老夫妇开垦荒地种菜，但遭遇大旱，种子不发芽，菜园荒芜，他们忧愁叹息。
[P7] 画面中，一对老夫妇正用扁担挑着水桶，艰难地行走，背景是一棵光秃秃的树和几只飞鸟，表现出干旱缺水的困境。
[P8] 老夫妇在菜园里发现两棵罕见的嫩芽，一粉一绿，他们欣喜若狂，精心照料，芽苗一天天长高。
[P9] 本页描述了两株嫩芽的生长过程：红芽长成结金瓜的藤蔓，绿芽长成结银豆角的藤蔓。老夫妇在瓜果成熟后，选择一个好天气去菜园采摘。
[P10] 老夫妇去菜园采摘，金瓜和银豆角自行落地或离秧，瓜壳和豆荚中分别躺着一个胖娃娃和一个嫩娃娃。
[P11] 老夫妇在菜园发现两个从瓜果中诞生的娃娃，娃娃们连声呼唤他们为爸爸妈妈，老夫妇惊慌地跑开。
[P12] 老夫妇被从瓜果中诞生的两个娃娃亲切地呼唤，最终接纳了他们，并为男孩取名金瓜儿，为女孩取名银豆儿，画面中老夫妇抱着两个娃娃，充满喜悦。
[P13] 本页描述金瓜儿和银豆儿在老夫妇的抚养下迅速长大，几年后已成青年，画面中两人挑着担子，充满生机地行走，象征着成长与希望。
[P14] 金瓜儿帮助父亲打理菜园，凭借出色的农活本领，将原本破败的菜园变成了生机勃勃、丰收富足的花果园。
[P15] 本页描述银豆儿帮助母亲打理家务，她勤劳聪慧，擅长针线、烹饪和农活，家中事务井井有条，老夫妇因此过上幸福美满的生活。画面中银豆儿正在喂鸡鸭，周围环境生机盎然。
[P16] 这一年，金瓜儿的菜园里长出了一个巨大的冬瓜，他将其命名为“冬瓜王子”，画面中金瓜儿正手持刻刀在冬瓜上刻字，周围藤蔓繁茂，充满生机。
[P17] 银豆儿的鸡群中出现了一只罕见的大公鸡，她为它取名为“雄鸡将军”，并挂上牌牌，画面中银豆儿正为公鸡佩戴牌牌，周围环境充满生机。
[P18] 李员外骑马路过铁柜山，看见老夫妇开垦的花果园，欲霸占并索要地租，老夫妇据理力争，指出此地是他们辛勤劳动四十年才开垦出来的。
[P19] 李员外要求老夫妇出示地契以证明土地所有权，老夫妇因无地契而陷入沉默，无法反驳。
[P20] 李员外以有地契为由，要求老夫妇三天内交出二十两金银，否则将赶他们出门。金瓜儿和银豆儿为救父母，决定去铁柜山寻宝，画面中他们正辛苦挖掘，手心起泡，汗流浃背。
[P21] 画面中金瓜儿和银豆儿正手持工具，艰难地在山间攀爬，背景是云雾缭绕的山峰和松树，表现他们为救父母而前往铁柜山寻宝的艰辛旅程。
[P22] 画面描绘了一只红色的公鸡立于山巅，背景是黄色的太阳和彩色的云纹，周围有松树和花草，整体风格为剪纸艺术，象征吉祥与希望。
[P23] 金瓜儿和银豆儿在铁柜山挖宝两天两夜未果，疲惫时一只大鸟出现，将山抬起并用巨石支撑，露出金山银山等宝藏。兄妹俩各取金银，认为足以交租，决定离开。
[P24] 画面描绘了一只红色的公鸡在黄色背景中飞翔，左侧有紫色和蓝色的山峦及彩色祥云，整体风格为剪纸艺术，象征吉祥与希望。
[P25] 兄妹俩在铁柜山发现支撑山体的巨石和大鸟，原来分别是他们自己种的大冬瓜和喂养的红公鸡，欣喜地认出这些神奇之物出自自家。
[P26] 第三天，李员外来收租，老夫妇拿出正好二十两的金银，李员外怀疑来源，老夫妇便如实告知了事情经过。
[P27] 李员外得知宝藏来源后，拒绝收金银，反而要以菜园子换取能支撑山体的冬瓜和公鸡，管家跟班强行抢走了这两样宝物。
[P28] 画面描绘了在弯月背景下，一只红色公鸡立于山巅，山体由紫色和蓝色云纹构成，山脚下有三个人物（疑似李员外及其随从）正搬运一个绿色大冬瓜，周围散落着金银财宝，整体风格为剪纸艺术，象征吉祥与希望。
[P29] 金瓜儿和银豆儿得知李员外夺走了他们的宝物后，愤怒地追了上去。李员外在铁柜山下贪婪地抢夺宝藏，兄妹俩赶到后，金瓜儿呼唤支山冬瓜，冬瓜听命滚回。
[P30] 画面描绘了李员外及其随从被巨大的冬瓜压在山下，三人倒地不起，表情惊恐，山体由蓝色云纹构成，顶部有粉色花朵，周围有绿色植物，整体风格为剪纸艺术，象征灾难与惩罚。
[P31] 银豆儿呼唤雄鸡将军，命令它将山压向偷宝的坏人。抓山鸡听命飞回，铁柜山从半空落下，将李员外及其随从永远压在山底。
